title: The Painted Letter
premise: When a flood damages the founder's mausoleum, coroner Bram Ishikawa supervises the exhumation of town patriarch Aldous Vane and finds the coffin empty — except for a single painted letter, the first stroke of an alphabet that matches letters hidden across Hollow Creek. Following them, Bram uncovers that Vane's celebrated death forty years ago was staged to cover his murder of a business partner, and that several founding families have been paying ever since to keep the secret buried. As the statute of limitations on the original crime nears expiry, someone begins killing the letter-keepers, and Bram realizes their own late mother was one of them. In the end, Bram exposes the surviving conspirator — the town's current mayor, Vane's granddaughter — choosing truth over the loyalty that protected her family, and lays their mother's complicity to rest beside the empty grave.
about_author: Ulyana Ishikawa is a former mortuary assistant turned novelist who grew up in a coastal logging town where everyone knew which graves held secrets. She writes quiet mysteries about small communities and the debts they never stop paying.

chapters.title: The Ground Gives Way
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Spring floods crack the Vane mausoleum, and the town council orders an exhumation Bram must legally oversee. The coffin lid comes up light. Empty, save for a hand-painted letter 'A' nailed inside. Beat: professional calm cracking into dread.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram walks the cemetery cataloguing who attended Vane's funeral, recalling how the whole town wept forty years ago. Deputy Reyes questions why Bram seems rattled. Beat: the weight of being the town's keeper of dead truths.

chapters.title: The Letter A
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Forensic analysis dates the painted letter to Vane's supposed death year. Bram finds a matching 'B' tucked in the historical society's mural during restoration. Beat: curiosity hardening into obsession.

chapters.title: What Mother Kept
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, with flashback. Sorting their late mother's effects, Bram finds a paint-stained rag and an old photograph of five founders' children. Beat: grief entangling with suspicion — was Mother one of the painters?

chapters.title: The Statute Clock
chapters.summary: Mayor Celeste Vane's POV. Celeste learns the exhumation may reopen the original case before limitations expire; she quietly pressures the council to rebury and seal. Beat: polished benevolence concealing panic.

chapters.title: C is for Candleworks
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Letter 'C' surfaces in the ruins of Vane's candle factory, beside scorch marks no fire report ever mentioned. An anonymous note warns Bram to stop digging. Beat: thrill curdling into fear.

chapters.title: Five Children of the Founder
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram interviews the last living member of the funeral party, ancient Harriet Osei, who recites the alphabet unprompted then refuses to say more. Beat: pity for witnesses who carried this too long.

chapters.title: D, Nailed Shut
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. Letter 'D' is found inside a sealed wall of the old schoolhouse; Reyes notices the nails match those in the coffin. Someone is planting letters now. Beat: the investigation turning on itself.

chapters.title: The First Death Again
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Archives reveal Vane's business partner Eli Marsh vanished the same week as Vane's 'death.' The closed case everyone swore by was never investigated at all. Beat: righteous anger at a town-wide lie.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Ledger
chapters.summary: Celeste's POV. Celeste meets with the two other surviving heirs; they argue over whether to destroy the remaining letters or let the statute run out. Beat: loyalty as inheritance, passed down like debt.

chapters.title: E in the Icehouse
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram finds 'E' in the disused icehouse along with Eli Marsh's wedding ring. The letters aren't a message — they're a confession someone scattered to be found after they died. Beat: sorrow reframing the mystery.

chapters.title: A Threat Made Flesh
chapters.summary: Harriet's POV. Harriet is found dead, her house ransacked, her copy of the photograph burned. Her death looks natural; Bram knows better. Beat: the cost of survival made literal.

chapters.title: F Is for Forgiveness
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Letter 'F,' painted in their mother's unmistakable hand, sits in Bram's own attic. Mother didn't just know — she helped hide the body. Beat: betrayal and love colliding.

chapters.title: The Mayor's Confessor
chapters.summary: Celeste's POV. Celeste visits Vane's grave at night and speaks aloud to him; it emerges she ordered the letters destroyed decades ago and failed. Beat: guilt wearing the mask of duty.

chapters.title: G, and the Man Who Waited
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. A drifter named Cole Marsh — Eli's grandson — arrives asking questions; he's been hunting the letters for years. Reluctantly, Bram shares what they know. Beat: wary alliance replacing isolation.

chapters.title: Hollow Creek's Honest Face
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. Reyes traces payments from the Vane estate to three families across four decades — hush money dressed as scholarships and pensions. Beat: disillusionment with the town's mythology.

chapters.title: The Expiry Date
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram calculates the statute expires in eleven days and petitions the district attorney to reopen the Marsh case; the DA stalls, visibly pressured. Beat: racing the clock against institutional silence.

chapters.title: I Is for Icarus Falls
chapters.summary: Cole's POV. Cole is attacked retrieving letter 'I' from the millpond; he survives but the letter is taken. Whoever holds it now controls the narrative. Beat: desperation sharpening the stakes.

chapters.title: The Last Letter
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram deduces the final letter, 'J,' is hidden in Vane's mausoleum itself — inside the false floor of the empty coffin, a full written confession naming his killer: his daughter, Celeste's mother. Beat: the trap snapping shut.

chapters.title: Statute of Limitations
chapters.summary: Bram and Reyes's alternating POV. Confronted at the mausoleum, Celeste admits her mother killed Eli and that the family staged Vane's death to flee, leaving the letters as her mother's penance. She burns nothing; she simply asks Bram to let it die. Beat: climax — truth offered a bribe of mercy.

chapters.title: What We Bury Together
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram files everything anyway; Celeste resigns rather than face trial, and the town convulses over its founding myth. Bram reinterred the coffin with the letters inside, a grave finally holding its truth. Beat: costly vindication.

chapters.title: The Painted Letter
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, epilogue. Months later, Bram paints a final letter — 'K,' for their mother, for keeping, for kindness — and buries it unmarked. Some cases close; some just get told honestly. Beat: quiet peace, truth chosen over loyalty, grief given a shape.
